The Ventura County Commercial Fishermen's Association member vessels will be operating within a 35 mile radius of San Nicholas Island between May 01, 2026 and February 28, 2027. Vessels can be expected in this area anytime wind and sea state is at Beaufort scale of 4 or less. Gear will be marked with a flagged highflyer, radar reflector, lights and buoys. Vessels can be contacted on VHF Channel 16 and 11. For further information please contact 805 448 4455, all mariners are advised to transit the area with caution.

Operations will involve the deployment and quarterly maintenance of in-water oceanographic data collection buoys at the following positions: Spotter 1 at 33.2965225, -117.4729195; Spotter 2 at 33.2900481, -117.4677166; and Spotter 3 at 33.2853513, -117.4626498. d: The Cabrillo Beach Yacht Club will sponsor the Holiday (Opti) Regatta Carrie #3 on December 5–6, 2026, from noon to 6 p.m. each day. Approximately 35 sailing dinghies will race on a course in the Los Angeles Harbor Shallow Water Habitat between Angel’s Gate and the Cabrillo Marina Entrance, centered at 33.708, -118.267. Mariners are requested to use caution when transiting in the vicinity of event participants. For more details or comments, contact Jonathan Mitsumori at (310) 831-4757. All mariners are advised to transit the area with caution.

San Diego Yacht Club is sponsoring the Hot Rum Regatta Series, involving approximately 50 sailing vessels racing primarily within San Diego Bay between Ballast Point and the Coronado Bridge. Operations will take place from 0800 to 1900 on November 7, November 21, and December 5, 2026. Latitude/longitude coordinates and VHF-FM channels monitored were not provided. For more information or to submit comments, contact Jeff Johnson at 619-758-6310. All mariners are advised to transit the area with caution.

The CRA Fall Regatta will occur in San Diego Bay on November 14, 2026, from 1100 to 1700. The event will involve approximately 50 sailing vessels. The race course will begin near the one-half-mile marker on Harbor Island, proceed to approximately the midpoint of Shelter Island, continue to the middle of San Diego Bay near Naval Base San Diego, then return to the one-half-mile marker on Harbor Island. Latitude and longitude coordinates and VHF-FM channels monitored were not provided. For further information or comments, contact Toralf Strand at 603-918-8060. All mariners are advised to transit the area with caution.

The U.S. Coast Guard has received a report of shoaling encroaching into the channel in the vicinity of Marina Del Rey entrance Light 4. Shoaling is reported with a depth observed of less than 7 feet at low tide at approximate position 33.95972, -118.46056. Sector LA/LB monitors VHF-FM channels 13 and 16. For more information, direct all questions and concerns to the Sector LA/LB Waterways Management Division at D11-SMB-LALB-wwm@uscg.mil. All mariners are advised to transit the area with caution.

The U.S. Coast Guard has received a report of shoaling in the vicinity of the Oceanside Harbor entrance near Oceanside South Jetty Light 2, located at approximately 33.20583° N, -117.40138° W. Mariners are advised that vessels with a draft of 10 feet or greater should remain to the west side of the channel during tides of less than +1 foot, as there is a risk of grounding on the east side of the channel during negative tides for drafts of 10 feet or greater. All mariners are urged to transit the area with caution. The relevant chart numbers for this area are US5CA77M (Del Mar Boat Basin) and US4CA73M (Gulf of Santa Catalina, Del Mar Boat Basin-Camp Pendleton). Questions or concerns can be directed to marineeventssd@uscg.mil

The Coast Guard received a report of a 26-foot sailing vessel sinking at the entrance to Santa Barbara Channel in the vicinity of 34.406717, -119.685167. All mariners are advised to transit the area with caution.
